'''Patrick Paul Billingsley''' (May 3, 1925 – April 22, 2011<ref>[http://mathdl.maa.org/mathDL/?pa=mathNews&sa=view&newsId=1110 Mathematician-Actor Patrick Billingsley Dies at 85]</ref><ref>[https://news.uchicago.edu/article/2011/04/29/patrick-billingsley-probability-theorist-and-actor-1925-2011 Patrick Billingsley, probability theorist and actor, 1925–2011]</ref>) was an American mathematician noted for his books in advanced [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]]. 

==Academic career==
Billingsley was born and raised in [[Sioux Falls, South Dakota]], and graduated from the [[United States Naval Academy]] in 1946. After earning a Ph.D. in mathematics at [[Princeton University]] in 1955, he was attached to the [[National Security Agency|NSA]] until his discharge from the Navy in 1957.  In 1958 he became a professor of mathematics and statistics at the [[University of Chicago]], where he served as chair of the Department of Statistics from 1980 to 1983, and retired in 1994.  In 1964–65 he was a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Fellow]] and visiting professor at the [[University of Copenhagen]].  In 1971–72 he was a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] and visiting professor at the [[University of Cambridge]] ([[Peterhouse, Cambridge|Peterhouse]]). From 1976 to 1979 he edited the [[Annals of Probability]].  In 1983 he was [[List of presidents of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics|president]] of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].  He was given the [[Lester R. Ford Award]] for his article "[[Prime number|Prime Number]]s and [[Brownian motion|Brownian Motion]]."<ref>Patrick Billingsley, [http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/prime-numbers-and-brownian-motion "Prime Numbers and Brownian Motion"], ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'', 1973, volume 80, pp. 1099–1115</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1986.<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter B|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|accessdate=July 20, 2011}}</ref>

In ''[[Young Men and Fire]]'', fellow University of Chicago professor [[Norman Maclean]] wrote about Billingsley that "he is a distinguished statistician and one of the best amateur actors I have ever seen".<ref>{{cite book|title=Young Men and Fire|first=Norman|last=Maclean|publisher=University of Chicago Press|year=2010|isbn=9780226501031|page=161|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SxKBcqWbAS8C&pg=PA161}}</ref>

==Books==
* ''Statistical Inference for Markov Processes'' (1961)
* ''Ergodic Theory and Information'' (1965)<ref>{{cite journal|author=Hajian, Arshag|title=Review: Patrick Billingsley, ''Ergodic and Information''|journal=Annals of Mathematical Statistics|year=1967|volume=38|issue=1|pages=285–286|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.aoms/1177699086|doi=10.1214/aoms/1177699086|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* ''[[Convergence of Probability Measures]]'' (1st Edition 1968, 2nd Edition 1999)<ref>{{cite journal|author=[[Richard M. Dudley|Dudley, R. M.]]|title=Review: P. Billingsley, ''Convergence of probability measures''|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|year=1971|volume=77|issue=1|pages=25–27|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183532614|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1971-12602-2|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* ''The Elements of Statistical Inference'' (with David L. Huntsberger, 1986)
* ''Probability and Measure'' (1st Edition 1976, 2nd Edition 1986, 3rd Edition, 1995, Anniversary Edition 2012 )

==Death==
He died in 2011, aged 85, in his [[Hyde Park, Chicago]] home. He was survived by his children, [[Franny Billingsley|Franny]], Patty, Julie, Marty and Paul, and his companion, Florence Weisblatt. His wife of nearly 50 years, social activist Ruth Billingsley, died in 2000.
